title: Softmax throughput: polynomial exp2, MUFU/FMA mix, conditional rescale

steps.title: Software exp2: range reduction + degree-3 polynomial; all exponentials move to the FMA pipeline
Mix MUFU and polynomial at a fixed ratio so both pipelines work at the same time
Conditional rescale: move the reference and correct O only when the max grows by more than τ = 8

cases.name: n1
cases.purpose: N=1: one CTA with two Q tiles; all 128 rows of tile 1 are out of bounds (TMA fills zeros, the store skips them); O = V, LSE = scale·q·k.

cases.name: one_block
cases.purpose: N=128: only tile 0 is valid; B>1, H>1: 4-D tensor map coordinates and grid mapping.

cases.name: two_tiles
cases.purpose: N=256 is exactly one tile pair with two K/V blocks, D=128: the Q coordinate of tile 1 (q0+128), the TMEM columns of S¹/O¹, and the position of P¹.

cases.name: tile1_tail
cases.purpose: N=200: tile 1 has only 72 valid rows, and the second K/V block has only 72 valid keys.

cases.name: tile1_position
cases.purpose: Non-causal, D=128, N=190: tile 1 has only 62 rows; V[j]=j/N exposes the packing order of P¹ (two adjacent keys swapped) and the TMEM columns of P¹.

cases.name: short_tail
cases.purpose: N=37, D=128: a row spans two 64-column panels; the 91 padding keys must be masked.

cases.name: scale
cases.purpose: scale=1, logits in the hundreds: scale must come from p.scale; without subtracting the max the result overflows.

cases.name: uniform
cases.purpose: Q=0: O is the mean of V, LSE = ln N. A missing or repeated multiply by α, or a wrong correction of ℓ, shows up here.

cases.name: ones_v
cases.purpose: V=1, 5 blocks, 3 CTA rows (tile pairs): the correction of O and the correction of ℓ must use the same α for O to equal 1; P of padding keys must be 0.

cases.name: position
cases.purpose: V[j]=j/N, 5 blocks: a wrong item index in the K/V ring buffer (K even, V odd) or a wrong parity reads another block.

cases.name: peaked
cases.purpose: D=128, 7 blocks, large logits: the max updates repeatedly, and the correction of O (α) must finish before PV.

cases.name: peaked_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: N=513 is 1 more than a multiple of the block size; the TMEM columns of O¹ depend on D.

cases.name: ring
cases.purpose: 12 blocks, 24 ring items: the ring buffer wraps several times; a wrong full/empty parity reads a stale block or hangs.

cases.name: peaked_fp16
cases.purpose: FP16, D=128, large logits and scale=1: for many elements x = (s − m)·scale·log₂e is far below −127, so the software exp2 must first clamp to −127; the max jumps often in the first few blocks.

cases.name: growing
cases.purpose: The max grows slowly, by about 1.4–4.3 per block (log₂ units); each per-block increase is below τ, but the total is far above τ: conditional rescale must compare with the "current reference", not with the previous block's max, or P exceeds the FP16 upper bound and becomes inf.

cases.name: growing_causal
cases.purpose: growing_max, causal, D=64: each row's max grows in different blocks, so within one warp some rows need a correction and others do not (warp vote).

cases.name: jump
cases.purpose: From key 650 (the middle of block 5) the logits jump up by about 145–430 (log₂ units): the jump block must move the reference and correct O (α ≈ 0), or P overflows to inf.

cases.name: jump_causal
cases.purpose: jump_max, BF16, causal, D=128: the jump starts at key 434; above 2^128 BF16/FP32 overflow too; rows before 434 do not see the jump, so within a tile some rows jump and some do not.

cases.name: medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=128: a full ping-pong over 8 blocks.

cases.name: medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=64, FP16.

cases.name: causal_n1
cases.purpose: Causal with N=1: the only query sees only itself.

cases.name: causal_pair
cases.purpose: Causal, one tile pair, large logits: block 2 of tile 0 is fully masked (must not produce NaN), and the diagonal block of tile 1 needs a mask.

cases.name: causal_tail
cases.purpose: Causal with N not a multiple of the block size: the diagonal mask and the tail mask apply at the same time; the second tile pair has only 44 rows.

cases.name: causal_n_bound
cases.purpose: Causal, N=640: the block count of the last tile pair (rows 512..767) is set by N (5 blocks), not by the diagonal (6 blocks); tile 1 of that pair is fully out of bounds, and the last block of tile 0 has both a diagonal mask and a tail mask.

cases.name: causal_position
cases.purpose: Causal, V[j]=j/N, D=128: a mask that is off by one reads values from future positions.

cases.name: causal_peaked
cases.purpose: Causal with large logits: masked elements in the diagonal block must not take part in the max.

cases.name: causal_uniform
cases.purpose: Causal with Q=0: O[i] is the mean of V[0..i], LSE[i] = ln(i+1).

cases.name: causal_ones_v
cases.purpose: Causal with V=1: O must equal 1, including row 0, which has only one key.

cases.name: causal_medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=128: tile pair p processes only blocks 0..2p+1.

cases.name: causal_medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=64.

cases.name: perf
cases.purpose: B·H=64, N=4096, D=128: 550 GFLOP, the same case as labs 22 and 34.

cases.name: perf_causal
cases.purpose: Same as above but causal: skipping blocks leaves about half the work.

cases.name: perf_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: the MMA per key is halved, so the exponentials (MUFU) take a larger share.

cases.name: perf_8k
cases.purpose: N=8192, D=128: 64 blocks per CTA; the main loop dominates, so the prologue/teardown matters least.
